newsitem.title: CHINA: China approves new airport for southern Guangzhou.
newsitem.headline: China approves new airport for southern Guangzhou.

text.p: China has given final clearance to construction of a 20 billion yuan ($2.4 billion) international airport in the southern city of Guangzhou, the China Daily said on Saturday.

Authorities in the city, capital of booming Guangdong province, would seek foreign financing to cover part of the cost of the airport, which was given final approval on Friday, the newspaper quoted city mayor Lin Shusen as saying.
"The new airport welcomes overseas firms to join hands in construction and management," Lin said.
Construction would begin within the year, he said.

Guangzhou city and the Civil Aviation Administration of China would provide direct investment for the project, which would be given a shareholding structure, the China Daily said but gave no other details of financing.
The new airport would require the construction of an expressway and elevated railway to the city centre and would force the relocation of 20,000 people, it said.

The airport would have three runways and annual capacity of 80 million passengers and 2.5 million tonnes of cargo. A first phase that included the construction of two of the runways would be completed in 2005, it said.
Guangzhou's existing Baiyun Airport handled 12.644 million passengers in 1996, it said.
